paper_title: Training and Evaluating with Human Label Variation An Empirical Study
caption: Soft accuracy and graphs for a binary classification problem on a single example where the true and the predicted judgement for the positive class is 0.5 and q respectively.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how two scalar quantities, “soft accuracy” and “PO-JSD,” vary as a function of a parameter \(q\) for a single binary-classification example. The x-axis is labeled \(q\) and uses a linear scale spanning approximately 0 to 1, with labeled ticks at 0.2 intervals (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). The y-axis is unlabeled, shown on a linear scale with values ranging roughly from 0.55 up to 1.0, with regularly spaced tick labels at 0.1 intervals (0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0). The “soft accuracy” curve is a solid blue line with no markers that increases linearly from about 0.55 near \(q\approx 0.05\) to 1.0 at \(q=0.5\), then decreases linearly back to about 0.55 near \(q\approx 0.95\), forming a symmetric triangular peak at \(q=0.5\). The “PO-JSD” curve is a solid orange line with no markers that starts around 0.8 near \(q\approx 0.05\), rises smoothly to a maximum near 1.0 at \(q=0.5\), and then declines smoothly back to around 0.8 near \(q\approx 0.95\), forming a symmetric, concave-down arc centered at \(q=0.5\).
